compatibility.destructive_changes: require a new major contract and an explicit migration
compatibility.rollback: every destructive migration requires a tested rollback or restore procedure

graph_schema.note: Read-only views over tables declared elsewhere in this contract. Nothing is materialized and no base table changes, so a consumer promotes to a commit carrying them without a migration.

appended_key_columns.note: Appended after the published columns of the four Discogs vertex views on every engine, including PostgreSQL 18 with the property graph switch off. Structural only: each restates its view's <entity>_id as text because PostgreSQL 19 beta 3 rejects a character varying vertex key. Not declared as a property graph property; <entity>_id keeps its published type.

property_graph.absent_on: PostgreSQL 18, and PostgreSQL 19 with the switch off
conditions: the SCHEMA_PROPERTY_GRAPH environment switch is enabled
property_graph.consumer_rule: consumers must not assume it exists; probe pg_class for a relation named catalog in schema graph, of relkind g, and fall back to the views, which are always present
property_graph.name: graph.catalog
property_graph.note: A SQL/PGQ declaration over the graph schema's views, applied after the rest of the PostgreSQL schema. A closed gate is logged and is not a failure. There is no IF NOT EXISTS for a property graph and this initializer never drops one, so an existing graph.catalog is left as it is and a changed declaration does not roll out on its own.

view_evolution.allowed: appending a column to the end of an existing view
view_evolution.engine_enforcement: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fails the statement outright rather than replacing the view
forbidden: renaming a view or a view column
view_evolution.migration: expand, migrate consumers, then contract, with a coordinated DROP ... CASCADE
